q: Ọ̀rọ̀-asojú-orúkọ wo ni a ń lò láti tẹnumọ́ ẹni tí ń sọ̀rọ̀?
explanation: 'Èmi' is the emphatic (independent) first-person singular pronoun used for stress or emphasis, unlike the clitic form 'Mo'.

q: Sílẹ́bù mélòó ni ó wà nínú ọ̀rọ̀-orúkọ yìí: 'À-mì-o-hùn'?
explanation: The word is broken down into four vowel-carrying units: À-mì-o-hùn.

q: Àmì ohùn wo ni ó wà lórí 'i' nínú ọ̀rọ̀ 'Èmi'?
explanation: In 'Èmi', the first 'E' has a low tone () and the 'i' has a mid tone, which is typically unmarked in Yoruba orthography.

q: Nínú fónẹ́tíìkì Yorùbá, fáwẹ́lì mélòó ni a ń pè ní 'Àránmú'?
explanation: Yoruba has five nasal vowels (fáwẹ́lì àránmú): an, ẹn, in, ọn, un.

q: Kí ni iṣẹ́ 'Èmi' nínú gbólóhùn yìí: 'Èmi ni ó lo sí ọjà'?
explanation: In this sentence, 'Èmi' functions as the Subject (Olùwà) of the sentence, specifically emphasized.

q: Báwo ni a ṣe ń kọ 'spirit' ní èdè Yorùbá pẹ̀lú àmì ohùn tí ó tọ́?
explanation: The word for spirit or soul is 'Ẹ̀mí' (low-high tone), while 'Èmi' is the pronoun 'I'.

q: Kí ni àmì ohùn 'Do' nínú gírámà Yorùbá?
explanation: The low tone is traditionally referred to as 'Do' and is represented by the grave accent ().

q: Kọ́nṣónáǹtì wo ni ó jẹ́ 'A-yan-nu' (Nasalized) nínú àwọn wọ̀nyí?
explanation: 'm' and 'n' are nasal consonants (kọ́nṣónáǹtì àránmú) because air escapes through the nose during their production.

q: Ìpín mélòó ni gírámà Yorùbá pín ọ̀rọ̀-asojú-orúkọ sí?
explanation: Yoruba pronouns are generally divided into two main categories: Short/Clitic forms and Emphatic/Independent forms.

q: Àpólà-ọ̀rọ̀ wo ni a rí nínú: 'Èmi àti Tọ́pẹ́'?
explanation: This is a Noun Phrase (Àpólà-orúkọ) formed by a conjunction joining two nominal items.

q: Kí ni a ń pè ní 'Tense' ní èdè Yorùbá?
explanation: 'Àsìkò' refers to Tense (Time of action), while 'Ìbá-ìṣe' refers to Aspect (Nature of action).

q: Èwo nínú àwọn wọ̀nyí ni kì í ṣe fáwẹ́lì ẹyọ (Oral vowel)?
explanation: 'in' is a nasal vowel, whereas a, e, and u are oral vowels (vocal cord vibration with mouth exit).

q: Ami ohùn wo ni a kò ní kọ sí orí ọ̀rọ̀-orúkọ nínú gírámà Yorùbá?
explanation: The mid tone (Re) is standardly left unmarked in written Yoruba, except in specific linguistic texts.

q: Kí ni iṣẹ́-oògùn 'Ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe' nínú gbólóhùn?
opts: Láti fihan ohun tí olùwà ṣe
explanation: A verb (Ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe) describes the action or state of the subject.

q: Ọ̀rọ̀ 'púpọ̀' jẹ́ _____.
explanation: 'Púpọ̀' (Many/Much) is an adjective (Ọ̀rọ̀-àpèjúwe) used to qualify nouns.

q: Báwo ni a ṣe ń kọ 'I am' ní kúkúrú nínú gírámà?
explanation: 'Mo ń' represents the first-person singular pronoun with the progressive marker 'ń'.

q: Nínú fọ́wẹ́lì, èwo ni a ń pè ní 'Fífẹ̀' (Open)?
explanation: 'a' is the low central open vowel in Yoruba phonology.

q: Kí ni Yorùbá ń pè ní 'Syllable'?
explanation: The term 'Sílẹ́bù' is the direct transliteration and grammatical term for Syllable in Yoruba.

q: Mélòó ni kọ́nṣónáǹtì inú èdè Yorùbá?
explanation: Standard Yoruba has 18 consonants: b, d, f, g, gb, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, r, s, ṣ, t, w, y.

q: Ọ̀rọ̀-asopọ̀ wo ni ó wà nínú: 'Èmi _____ rẹ̀'?
explanation: 'Àti' is the standard conjunction for 'and' used to join two equal nominal items.

q: Báwo ni a ṣe ń kí ènìyàn tí ó bẹ̀rẹ̀ iṣẹ́ tuntun?
explanation: 'Ẹ kú oríire' is the general greeting for success or good fortune, including a new job.

q: Kí ni iṣẹ́-oògùn 'Ọ̀rọ̀-atọ́ka'?
opts: Láti fihàn ibi tí nkan wà
explanation: A preposition (Ọ̀rọ̀-atọ́ka) indicates the relationship (direction, location) of a noun to other words.

q: Fáwẹ́lì wo ni ó máa ń bẹ̀rẹ̀ ọ̀rọ̀-orúkọ nínú èdè Yorùbá?
explanation: Most Yoruba nouns begin with an oral vowel (fáwẹ́lì ẹyọ). Nasal vowels never begin a word in Yoruba.

q: Èwo ni àmì-òkè nínú àwọn wọ̀nyí?
opts.explanation: The high tone (Mi) is represented by the acute accent (/) rising from left to right.

opts.q: Kí ni ìhun gbólóhùn yìí: 'Èmi ra a'?
opts.explanation: Structure: Èmi (Subject) + ra (Verb) + a (Object).

opts.q: Ta ni Olúwa Ẹ̀mí nínú ìgbàgbọ́ Yorùbá?
opts.explanation: Olodumare is the supreme creator and the one who puts 'Ẹ̀mí' (the breath of life) into the 'Ara' (body).

opts.q: Kí ni Yorùbá ń pè ní 'Naming Ceremony'?
opts.explanation: The naming ceremony is called 'Ìsọmọlórúkọ', where a child is given their identities.

opts.q: Mélòó ni ọjọ́ orúkọ fún ọmọkùnrin nínú àṣà Yorùbá àtijọ́?
opts.explanation: Traditionally, boys were named on the 9th day, while girls were named on the 7th day.

opts.q: Èwo nínú àwọn wọ̀nyí ni ohun èlò ìsọmọlórúkọ fún 'Sweetness'?
opts.explanation: Honey (Oyin) is used to symbolize that the child's life will be sweet and pleasant.

opts.q: Báwo ni a ṣe ń kí ènìyàn tó ń ṣiṣẹ́ lọ́wọ́?
opts.explanation: 'Ẹ kú iṣẹ́' is the specific greeting used to acknowledge someone engaged in labor or activity.

opts.q: Kí ni iṣẹ́ 'Orí' nínú àyànmọ́ ènìyàn?
opts.explanation: In Yoruba belief, 'Orí' is the inner head or spiritual essence that carries an individual's destiny.

opts.q: Àpín-orí ni a tún mọ̀ sí _____.
opts.explanation: 'Àpín-orí' refers to the choosing of destiny at the point of creation, synonymous with 'Àyànmọ́'.

opts.q: Ta ni aṣojú Olódùmarè lórí ilẹ̀ ayé?
opts.explanation: The King (Ọba) is regarded as the 'Igbá-kejì Òrìṣà' (second to the gods) and God's representative on earth.

opts.q: Kí ni 'Orìkì'?
opts.explanation: Orìkì are praise poems or appellations used to celebrate individuals, lineages, or deities.

opts.q: Èwo nínú àwọn wọ̀nyí ni kì í ṣe Òrìṣà Yorùbá?
opts.explanation: Zeus is a Greek deity, not part of the Yoruba pantheon (Òrìṣà).

opts.q: Kí ni iṣẹ́ Ògún?
opts.explanation: Ogun is the deity of iron, war, and technology.

opts.q: Báwo ni a ṣe ń kí ẹni tó ń sunkún ọ̀fọ̀?
opts.explanation: 'Ẹ kú ọ̀rọ̀' is the condolence greeting for someone mourning or facing a serious matter.

opts.q: Parí òwe yìí: 'Iṣẹ́ ni oògùn _____'?
opts.explanation: The proverb 'Iṣẹ́ ni oògùn ìyà' translates to 'Work is the antidote to poverty/suffering'.

opts.q: Kí ni 'Ìdána' nínú ìgbéyàwó?
opts.explanation: Ìdána is the engagement ceremony where the bride price/gifts are presented.

opts.q: Èwo ni orúkọ àmúmọ̀-wáyé fún ọmọ tí a bí pẹ̀lú kòpò mọ́rùn?
opts.explanation: Àìná is a child born with the umbilical cord around the neck.

opts.q: Èwo ni ohun tí a ń lò fún 'Ìtura' nínú ìkíni?
opts.explanation: Water (Omi) is offered to visitors first to symbolize hospitality and relief (Ìtura).

opts.q: Kí ni ìtumọ̀ 'Àbíkú'?
opts: Ọmọ tó ń kú tí ó sì ń padà wá
opts.explanation: Àbíkú refers to 'one who is born to die', a child believed to repeatedly cycle through birth and death.

opts.q: Kí ni iṣẹ́-oògùn 'Obì' nínú àṣà Yorùbá?
opts.explanation: Kola nut (Obì) is used for divination (to seek knowledge/answers) and as a sign of hospitality.

opts.q: Orúkọ wo ni a ń pe ọmọ tí a bí lẹ́yìn ìbejì?
opts.explanation: Ìdòwú is the name given to the child born immediately after a set of twins.

opts.q: Kí ni 'Ẹ̀kọ́-ilé'?
opts: Ẹ̀kọ́ tí a kọ́ ní ilé-ìwé
Ìwà àti àṣà tí òbí ń kọ́ ọmọ
opts.explanation: Home training (Ẹ̀kọ́-ilé) involves the moral and cultural values parents pass to their children.

opts.q: Ta ni ó kọ ìwé 'Ògbójú Ọdẹ nínú Igbó Irúnmalẹ̀'?
opts.explanation: D.O. Fagunwa is the pioneer of the Yoruba novel, famous for this work.

opts.q: Kí ni 'Àlọ̀ Àpagbe'?
opts.explanation: Àlọ̀ Àpagbe refers to folktales that include songs where the audience joins in the refrain.

opts.q: Èwo ni kò sí nínú lítíréṣọ̀ àtẹnudẹ́nu (Oral Literature)?
opts.explanation: A novel is written literature, while the others originated as oral forms.

opts.q: Kí ni 'Ewì'?
opts: Ọ̀rọ̀ a-kọ-lù-pọ̀ tí ó ní ìlù
opts.explanation: Poetry (Ewì) is rhythmic, chanted, or spoken literature with specific structures and aesthetics.

opts.q: Ta ni akọni nínú 'Ògbójú Ọdẹ'?
opts.explanation: Akara-oogun is the central hero who narrates his journeys into the forest.

opts.q: Fáwẹ́lì mélòó ni ó wà nínú 'Ẹ̀-mí'?
opts.explanation: It contains two vowels: 'Ẹ' and 'i'.

opts.q: Èwo ni 'Figure of speech' fún 'Simile' ní Yorùbá?
opts.explanation: Simile is 'Ìfiwé tààrà', comparing two things using 'bí' or 'dàbí'.

opts.q: Kí ni ìtumọ̀ 'Àyànmọ́'?
opts.explanation: Destiny or fate is known as 'Àyànmọ́' in Yoruba philosophy.

opts.q: Orúkọ-àbíkú wo ni 'Dúrójaye'?
opts.explanation: Durojaye means 'Stay and enjoy life', given to Abiku to plead with them to survive.

opts.q: Ìpín mélòó ni lítíréṣọ̀ Yorùbá ní?
opts.explanation: Literature is divided into two: Lítíréṣọ̀ Àtẹnudẹ́nu (Oral) and Lítíréṣọ̀ Àtinúdá (Written).

opts.q: Èwo ni 'Eré Oníṣe'?
opts.explanation: Drama is called 'Eré Oníṣe' because it involves performance and action.

opts.q: Kí ni 'Ìyàtọ̀'?
opts.explanation: 'Ìyàtọ̀' means Difference.

opts.q: Ta ni a mọ̀ sí 'Bale'?
opts.explanation: A 'Baálẹ̀' is the head or traditional ruler of a village or settlement.

opts.q: Èwo ni àmì-ìsàlẹ̀?
opts.explanation: The low tone is represented by the backslash or grave accent (\).

opts.q: Kí ni Yorùbá ń pè ní 'Adverb'?
opts.explanation: While often categorized with adjectives, 'Ọ̀rọ̀-atẹnumọ́' or specific adverbial phrases serve this function.

opts.q: Èwo ni fáwẹ́lì nasal 'un'?
opts.explanation: In Yoruba orthography, 'un' represents the high back nasal vowel.

opts.q: Parí òwe yìí: 'Bí ẹ̀mí bá wà, _____ á wà'?
opts.explanation: The proverb means 'If there is life, there is hope' (Ìrètí).

opts.q: Kí ni Yorùbá ń pè ní 'Alphabet'?
opts.explanation: The Yoruba alphabet system is called 'Abidì'.

opts.q: Kí ni iṣẹ́ 'Èmi' nínú èdè?
opts.explanation: The primary role of 'Èmi' is the identification of the speaker.

opts.q: Ìgbà mélòó ni a ń sẹ 'Ìsọmọlórúkọ'?
opts.explanation: Depending on gender or local tradition, 7th, 8th, or 9th day are all common naming days.

opts.content: Èmi ni mo mọ ohun tí mo fẹ́ nínú ayé. Ẹ̀mí ènìyàn ṣe pàtàkì ju wúrà àti fàdákà lọ. Bí a bá ní ẹ̀mí, a ní ohun gbogbo. Ìwà rere ni ohun tí ó ń jẹ́ kí ẹ̀mí ènìyàn sinmi nígbà tí ó bá padà sí ọ̀dọ̀ Ẹlẹ́dàá. Yorùbá gbàgbọ́ pé ayé ni ọjà, ọ̀run ni ilé. Nítorí náà, ẹ jẹ́ kí a hùwà rere.

questions.q: Gẹ́gẹ́ bí passage yìí, kí ni ó ṣe pàtàkì ju wúrà lọ?
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states that human life (Ẹ̀mí) is more important than gold and silver.

questions.q: Ibi wo ni passage yìí pè ní 'ọjà'?
questions.explanation: It uses the philosophical metaphor 'Ayé ni ọjà' (The world is a marketplace).

questions.q: Kí ni ẹ̀mí ènìyàn máa ń ṣe lẹ́yìn ikú?
opts: Ó ń padà sí ọ̀dọ̀ Ẹlẹ́dàá
Kò sí ohun tó ń ṣẹlẹ̀
questions.explanation: The text states the soul returns to the Creator (Ẹlẹ́dàá) after life.

questions.q: Ọ̀rọ̀-asojú-orúkọ wo ni ó bẹ̀rẹ̀ passage yìí?
questions.explanation: The passage starts with the word 'Èmi'.

questions.q: Kí ni àmì ohùn tó wà lórí 'ọ' nínú ọ̀rọ̀ 'ọjà'?
questions.explanation: In 'ọjà', the 'ọ' has a mid tone (unmarked) and the 'à' has a low tone.
